text:
ryan: Heads-up — perf alert from canary: host CPU p95 decode up ~9% after last ingress tweak. traces look like a stream of many tiny HTTP/1.1 requests rather than fewer HTTP/2 frames.
marta: can you paste the top callstacks?
jia: I grabbed a condensed flame:
```
ingress::read_small_frames -> 22%
parse::header_state_machine -> 14%
tokenizer::prefetch_and_tokenize -> 18%
kvcache::lease_miss_backoff -> 9%
runtime::dispatch_writev -> 11%
```
ryan: also seeing lots of short-lived connections in tcp_conn table. connection reuse metric down 30%.
ade: recent change was http1 aggressive flush for low-latency (PR #4121). It forces flush on request boundary which means write coalesce disabled for http1 paths.
marta: that explains the v small writes. could be increasing syscall/writev overhead and causing ingress reads to be more fragmented.
perf-bot: quick diff: writev ops +x3, syscalls/sec +80%.
jia: TTL note: kvcache leasing code uses per-connection affinity token which we rotate on reconnect. with reuse down, lookups become cold.
ade: proposed mitigations: (A) re-enable coalesce for http1 but keep low-latency timer, (B) add small-buffer aggregator in ingress that merges consecutive writes within 500us, or (C) move prefetch tokenization earlier (accept body, batch tokens across concurrent short requests).
ryan: (C) worries me — introduces cross-request batching which can change semantics if there's per-request state. but maybe for plain text requests it's safe behind a flag.
marta: let's try quick A first on canary and measure. Jia, can you run a synthetic that simulates 200rps of tiny 10-20 byte prompts to exercise kernel selection?
jia: running tracegen with --len-dist=short --concurrency=250 now. planning to test kernel thresholds for n_tokens in {4,8,16,32}.
perf-bot: tracegen run queued -> jobs/6280000001/tracegen/short-run.json
ade: kernel-selector detail — our backend picks a "micro" kernel for seq<=8, a "wide" kernel for seq>8. micro kernel has worse per-token throughput but lower memory. If current workload sits at median 7 tokens we get micro kernel and higher CPU. nudging batch size to push median over 8 moves to wide kernel.
ryan: could we tweak batching heuristic: when micro kernel is selected and queue depth > 40, temporarily bump batch target by +2 tokens to try and cross threshold?
marta: (typo) marta: I like that adaptive nudge idea. add guard to avoid increasing latency for small-latency SLO customers.
perf-bot: synthetic results: baseline: median tokens=7 -> micro kernel; p95 CPU +10%. With batch-nudge to target 9 tokens -> median tokens=9 -> wide kernel selected -> p95 CPU down ~7%, p95 latency improved 5%. writev rate unchanged.
jia: interestingly kvcache miss-rate also fell 6% under batch-nudge, probably due to fewer concurrent ephemeral connections because responses finished faster.
ade: next: implement ingress coalesce toggle on canary (A) and kernel-nudge (B) as two orthogonal flags. roll to 5% each.
marta: owners?
ryan: I'll flip coalesce toggle and watch TCP reuse.
jia: I'll land kernel-nudge change behind feature flag and add histogram for selected kernel vs batch size.
ade: I'll add the small-buffer aggregator prototype as a fallback if A+B don't fully solve it.
perf-bot: canary rollout: coalesce-toggle=on to 5% at t=6280000016. kernel-nudge rollout=on to 5% at t=6280000017.
infra-bot: created perf run dashboard -> dashboards/perf/6280000001-small-write-incident
ryan: early canary numbers (10m): coalesce toggle reduced writev syscalls by ~60% and connection reuse by +22%. kernel-nudge reduced selected micro-kernel fraction from 82% -> 28% on those hosts.
marta: nice. any KV eviction change?
jia: eviction spikes dropped; lease_miss_backoff occurrences down 45% in canary window. KV hit rate up ~4%.
ade: note: need to be careful for mobile clients that rely on immediate flush semantics. coalesce toggle should respect a "no-coalesce" header or flag for clients that request instant flush.
ryan: agreed. let's ship this to 25% for 12h soak, but keep kernel-nudge in a conservative ramp for customers with strict latency SLOs. add alert rule: if p95 latency increases >8% for any customer segment within 30m, rollback.
perf-bot: added rule perf/alerts/kv-eviction-spike and perf/alerts/p95-latency-regression.
marta: follow-ups: (1) postmortem-style doc with root cause & fixes, (2) evaluate preparse sidecar prototype, (3) long-term: consider merging small-buffer aggregator into http layer with option to coalesce across requests for plaintext endpoints.
ryan: I'll draft the doc after 12h soak. thanks all. :shipit:
